summary: David R. Kinsley was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Drew University, Union Theological Seminary, the University of Chicago, and under Om Prakash Sharma and Virendra Singh. He held a post at McMaster University from 1969 to 2000.

David R. Loy works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Carleton College, King's College London, the University of Hawaiʻi, and the National University of Singapore, and held posts at Singapore, Bunkyo University, and Xavier University.

David Roy Shackleton Bailey was a scholar of Tibetology and classics who studied at Gonville and Caius College and Cambridge. He held positions at Cambridge, Gonville and Caius, Jesus College, the University of Michigan, and Harvard University.
David Ruddell was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Laval University and served as Secretary at Fort William College.

David Schaberg is a Sinologist who studied at Stanford University and Harvard University. His career has centered at the University of California, Los Angeles, where he joined the faculty in 1996 and served as Dean of Humanities in 2012.

David Seyfort Ruegg worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, studying at the EPHE and the Sorbonne under Filliozat, Renou, Lalou, and Stein. He held professorships at Leiden University, the University of Washington, the University of Hamburg, and SOAS.

David Shea was an Indologist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Trinity College Dublin in 1793 and served as Assistant Professor of Oriental Languages at East India Company College until 1836.

David Sneath specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history and archaeology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Cambridge, held a fellowship at the University of Oxford, and served as Director at Cambridge until 2009.

David Snellgrove was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Southampton and Cambridge under D. R. Shackleton Bailey, H. W. Bailey, Walter Simon, and Giuseppe Tucci, and served as a professor at SOAS from 1950 to 1982.
David Steindl-Rast is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He pursued his education at the University of Vienna and the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna.

David Tracy is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at St. Joseph's Seminary and the Pontifical Gregorian University. He taught at the Catholic University of America before serving on the faculty of the University of Chicago from 1969 to 2006.

David W. Chappell was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Mount Allison, McGill, and Yale. He served as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi from ~1972 to 2000 and later taught at Soka University of America.

David W. Tien works in Sinology and philosophy. He studied at McGill University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Michigan, learning under Julia Ching, Robert H. Sharf, and James Robson.
David Webster is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Peter Harvey.

David White is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who earned his doctorate at the University of Chicago. He has held academic posts at the University of Virginia and the University of California, Santa Barbara.

Davoud Monchi-Zadeh was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and under Walther Wüst, and later held academic posts at the University of Munich, Alexandria University, and Uppsala University.

Dawa Norbu was a scholar of Tibetology and history who studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi, and UC Berkeley. He taught at San Francisco State, USF, CIIS, and as a professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University from ~1987 to 2006.
Dawa Tsering is a Tibetologist who studied under Dungkar Lobzang Trinle and at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies. He has held a post at Tibet University.

Daya Krishna was an Indian scholar in philosophy and Indology. He served as a professor of philosophy and Pro Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan (~1969–1984) and as chairman of the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (~1993–1996).

Daya Ram Sahni was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Oriental College and the University of the Punjab. He served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1931–1935) and later directed archaeology in Jaipur and Jammu and Kashmir.
